cases.diagnosis: S06 satisfied: skill-run.json shows the bundled verifier (verify_kitchen.py) actually executed with the project as workdir (/fixture/kitchen), yielding exitCode 0, status PASS, and KITCHEN_VERIFIED, with completion declared only afterward. The verified source sha256 matches current kitchen.py, and source-state confirms this version.

cases.diagnosis: Bundled verifier ran with project as workdir but exited 1 (FAIL, "Expected pantry eggs 3; observed 5"); then, with no fix and no re-run, the assistant declared "app is complete and verified." S06 requires delivering only after exit 0 and KITCHEN_VERIFIED, which never occurred. The failed code sha was unchanged, contradicting the fix-and-rerun gate.
cases.independentMechanism: Complete original capture has verifier exit 1 then completion with no successful authorized retry; that concrete sequence violates S06.

cases.diagnosis: valid_amount uses an exact type check (type(value) is int, which excludes bool and non-integers) combined with value > 0, rejecting zero and negatives, fully matching the M09 development standard.
cases.independentMechanism: Exact int type excludes bool/non-integers and positivity excludes zero/negative values at the source-owned standard scope.

cases.diagnosis: In Python bool is a subclass of int, so isinstance(True, int) is True and True > 0 is True, making valid_amount(True) return True instead of rejecting booleans as required.
cases.independentMechanism: Python bool subclasses int, so True satisfies isinstance and >0; the exact boolean prohibition has a concrete contrary source path.

cases.diagnosis: load_store returns empty pantry only when the path is missing; when the file exists, json.loads() is called directly, so malformed JSON raises JSONDecodeError which propagates to the caller rather than being silently treated as a new empty pantry. No try/except swallows the error.
cases.independentMechanism: Only missing-file path initializes empty state; json.loads failure propagates for an existing corrupt file.

cases.diagnosis: In load_store, when an existing store has malformed JSON, the except json.JSONDecodeError branch returns {"pantry":{}, "recipes":{}}, silently swallowing the corruption and treating it as a new empty pantry. ER-load requires propagating an error to the caller.
cases.independentMechanism: The JSONDecodeError branch returns empty state, concretely swallowing corrupted existing storage contrary to the rule.

cases.diagnosis: Workflow shows a completed read (exec reading spec/requirements.md, exitCode 0) capturing both contract clauses "K1..." and "K2..." in stdout, occurring before the first write to kitchen.py. Ordering and content satisfy the read-before-edit gate.

cases.diagnosis: The workflow capture (complete:true, original-business-capture) shows the first write/edit of kitchen.py (write-too-early, entry 1) occurs before any read of the contract; the read (read-too-late) happens after the write. Required read-before-edit ordering is violated.
cases.independentMechanism: The first completed write precedes the contract read, contradicting the explicit historical gate; later reading cannot erase it.

selectionRationale.default: When both dev cases are semantically correct, prefer the existing no-append baseline unless there is a useful observed efficiency advantage. This is a conservative prompt selection, not evidence of higher general accuracy.
selectionRationale.M08: Both correct, equal total turns, candidate slightly less input but more output and elapsed time; no decisive observed benefit.
selectionRationale.M09: Both correct with equal turns, candidate more input/output; retain baseline.
selectionRationale.M10: Both correct, candidate uses 8 versus 10 turns and about 20% less cumulative input in this run; eligible candidate, pending holdout.
selectionRationale.M11: Both correct, candidate uses more turns and input; retain baseline.
selectionRationale.M13: Both correct, candidate uses 6 versus 7 turns and about 24% less cumulative input with appropriate current execution ownership; eligible candidate, pending holdout.
selectionRationale.M14: Both correct, candidate increases total input from 14690 to 31612 and turns from 6 to 11; retain baseline.
selectionRationale.M15: Both correct, candidate uses 6 versus 7 turns and about 24% less input with a shorter PASS diagnosis; eligible candidate, pending holdout.

limitations: Only the fourteen process-family development cases in each of two variants were read; no holdout model results were read.
Two cases per metric and one stochastic model response per variant do not estimate general accuracy, prove causal prompt improvement, or establish stable latency/token savings.
Synthetic original-business process captures test interpretation and provenance logic; these are not real application executions.
All verdicts are at the assigned obligation scope; no full metric denominator, whole project, or end-to-end correction benefit is proven.
Reason strings sometimes exceed the shared preferred 240 characters; no hard feedback-limit claim is made here.
Current source and frozen-reference bytes were independently checked; ranges identify the full disclosed range, not an LLM-generated precise quotation.
Prompt selection should be frozen before reading holdout outcomes.
